ruling: F-A2 (Q-L1-01): chart_divisionals unique key gains fact_subject (seven columns)
description: F-A2 (PR #2858; migrations 1222 / 1223; ga_vargas writer). The chart_divisionals unique index and the data-plane capture trigger gain a seventh column, fact_subject, so rows that differ only in fact_subject no longer collide on one stored row (under the six-column key the ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING silently dropped all but the first). Effect on the canonical chart (production 24,392 chart_divisionals rows; the rehearsal baseline built from main has the identical row count and structure): 24,392 -> 38,596 stored rows, +14,204 = varga_ashtakavarga +13,200 (30 vargas x 8 grahas x 5 ayanamshas = 1,200 keys, each 1 -> 12 rows, one per sign: +440 per varga) + varga_house_lord +750 (+25 per varga: the five two-sign lords gain a row per (varga, ayanamsha)) + varga_d30_lord_per_amsa +250 + scope_cap +4 (the six INVARIANT sentinels, of which four collided: stored 2 -> 6). No row of any other category appears, disappears or changes value. DETECTOR VIEW: the detector keys chart_divisionals rows by (ayanamsha, varga, graha, category, fact_key) and counts a CHANGED KEY once, so the row-level figures above read as occurrence-count changes: varga_ashtakavarga 1,200 keys (1 -> 12) and, because the old single row (sign Aries on every key, stored by the six-column writer) pairs with the alphabetically first new sign (Aquarius) in the sorted occurrence pairing, also 1,200 value changes; varga_house_lord 750 keys (1 -> 2); varga_d30_lord_per_amsa 50 keys; scope_cap 1 key (1 -> 5). CORRECTION to the figure quoted in the hook request: varga_ashtakavarga is +440 per varga over 30 vargas = +13,200, not '+440 x 32 vargas = +14,080' (the stored table has 30 vargas). The total 14,204 is the stored difference and matches 13,200 + 750 + 250 + 4. Canonical chart only: Abhinandan and Kiran hold stale generations (23,542 rows) and are S-L1b. The scope_cap entry is also declared by ga_vargas_invariant_sentinels.json (integration branch, #2960); both count the same change.
